dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: Your colleague calls the proposal ambitious. What does that imply?
dialogue.text_he: העמית מכנה את ההצעה שאפתנית. מה משתמע מכך?

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: It may signal admiration, concern about feasibility, or both.
dialogue.text_he: זה עשוי להביע הערכה, חשש לגבי היתכנות או שניהם.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: Would you report that as qualified support?
dialogue.text_he: האם תדווחו על כך כתמיכה מסויגת?

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: Only if the surrounding conversation supported that interpretation.
dialogue.text_he: רק אם ההקשר בשיחה תומך בפרשנות הזאת.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: How could you clarify without putting her on the spot?
dialogue.text_he: איך תבררו בלי להעמיד אותה במצב לוחץ?

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: I would ask which assumptions she would want checked first.
dialogue.text_he: אשאל אילו הנחות היא הייתה רוצה לבדוק תחילה.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: How would you correct the volunteers’ expectations?
dialogue.text_he: איך תתקנו את ציפיות המתנדבים?

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: I would state that funding remains undecided and further evidence is required.
dialogue.text_he: אציין שהמימון טרם הוכרע ושנדרשות ראיות נוספות.

units.passage_en:
At the end of a meeting about extending the town market, the finance officer described the proposal as ambitious. The organiser heard enthusiasm and later told volunteers that funding was almost certain. A colleague heard a warning and advised postponing publicity. Both interpretations went beyond what the officer had explicitly said.

The word itself could express admiration, concern about feasibility, or a mixture of the two. Context mattered. Earlier, the officer had asked whether income estimates included bad-weather days. She had also praised the plan's support for small businesses. Her response was neither an unconditional promise nor a straightforward rejection.

Rather than asking whether she had been positive or negative, the organiser sent a more useful follow-up. He summarised his understanding: the purpose appeared worthwhile, but the revenue assumptions needed further testing. He asked which evidence would allow the finance team to assess the proposal and whether any funding decision had actually been made.

The officer confirmed that no decision had been reached. She requested a lower-income scenario and a revised estimate for security costs. The organiser corrected his message to the volunteers before they booked additional equipment.

Reading between the lines can help an experienced listener notice reservations. It cannot turn an inference into a fact. In this case, the most competent response was to hold two plausible interpretations in mind, check the surrounding evidence, and formulate a question that made the practical uncertainty explicit without demanding an immediate endorsement.

passage_questions.question_en: What central distinction does the text make?
passage_questions.answer_en: An inferred intention is not an explicit commitment.

passage_questions.question_en: Which scenario did the officer request?
passage_questions.answer_en: A lower-income scenario.

passage_questions.question_en: Which cost needed a revised estimate?
passage_questions.answer_en: Security costs.

passage_questions.question_en: Who does Her refer to in paragraph two?
passage_questions.answer_en: The finance officer.

passage_questions.question_he: למה השאלה חיובית או שלילית פחות מועילה?
passage_questions.question_en: Why was positive or negative a less useful question?
passage_questions.answer_en: It reduced mixed reservations to a label instead of clarifying decision requirements.

passage_questions.question_he: מה אפשר לדווח למתנדבים כעובדה מאומתת?
passage_questions.question_en: What could be reported to volunteers as confirmed?
passage_questions.answer_en: No funding decision had been made and further evidence was requested.

units.roleplay_prompt_he: המורה מגיב להצעה בשבח עמום ושאלה ביקורתית. הציגו שתי פרשנויות סבירות, שאלו שאלה מבהירה וסכמו רק התחייבויות מפורשות.
units.model_response_en: I took your comments as recognition of the proposal's potential, alongside reservations about the income estimates. However, I do not want to imply that you have endorsed it. Could you clarify which assumptions need further evidence and whether a decision is expected after that review? Until then, I will describe the discussion as exploratory and avoid asking volunteers to make commitments on the basis of inferred support.
units.writing_prompt_he: כתבו ניתוח בן 220–260 מילים של תגובה עמומה: שתי פרשנויות, ראיות הקשר, מגבלת ההסקה, שאלת בירור וסיכום מעשי.

language_focus.rule_he: might have ואחריה past participle מציגה פרשנות אפשרית לאירוע או לכוונה בעבר. היא אינה קובעת שהפרשנות נכונה. must have מביעה מסקנה חזקה יותר בעיני הדובר. בקריאת כוונה משתמעת כדאי להבחין בין מה שנאמר במפורש לבין מה שאנו משערים.
language_focus.example_en: The organiser might have intended this as a reminder.
language_focus.contrast_en: The organiser must have intended this as a reminder.
language_focus.prompt_he: ייתכן שהמארגן התכוון לתזכורת, אבל כוונתו אינה ידועה. נסחו בעזרת might have ו־intend.

units.passage_en:
Two reports about a revised bus network appeared to reach opposite conclusions. The transport authority announced that average journey times had fallen. A neighbourhood association described longer, less reliable journeys and demanded that the old routes be restored. A local editor wanted a summary that explained the discrepancy rather than merely placing the claims side by side.

The authority used ticket records from all daytime passengers during the first month. Its figures suggested that direct journeys along the main corridor had become quicker. However, the calculation excluded waiting before the first ticket was scanned and did not cover services after nine at night.

The association interviewed forty residents in two outer neighbourhoods. Most worked late shifts or depended on a connecting service. Their accounts described missed connections and longer waits. The interviews revealed problems the authority's measure might overlook, although they could not establish how common those problems were across the whole network.

The editor's synthesis distinguished between an aggregate improvement and its distribution. Faster daytime journeys on a busy route could coexist with worse journeys for a smaller group. The sources therefore converged on the existence of substantial changes while diverging in the passengers and parts of the journey they examined.

The resulting article did not announce that both reports were equally complete or that neither was useful. It recommended collecting total door-to-door travel times, including late services, before judging the redesign as a whole. Reconciling the evidence meant explaining its boundaries, not averaging incompatible claims into a vague compromise.

passage_questions.question_en: How were the reports reconciled?
passage_questions.answer_en: They measured different passenger groups and parts of a journey.

passage_questions.question_en: Which time was excluded from the authority's measure?
passage_questions.answer_en: Waiting before the first ticket scan.

passage_questions.question_en: How many residents were interviewed?
passage_questions.answer_en: Forty.

passage_questions.question_en: What does Its refer to in paragraph two?
passage_questions.answer_en: The transport authority's.

passage_questions.question_he: למה לא הוכח שהבעיות שכיחות בכל הרשת?
passage_questions.question_en: Why was network-wide prevalence not established?
passage_questions.answer_en: The interviews covered a small selected group in two neighbourhoods.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה מדד משותף מוצע לבדיקה הבאה?
passage_questions.question_en: Which common measure is proposed for further assessment?
passage_questions.answer_en: Total door-to-door journey times, including late services.

units.passage_en:
The water supplier discovered a fault in a monitoring sensor. Its engineers needed a detailed internal note explaining the equipment, the checks already completed and the remaining uncertainty. Residents needed a different message: whether their water supply was affected, what they should do, and when reliable information would follow.

An initial public draft copied the engineering note almost directly. It described intermittent telemetry failure and diagnostic procedures without explaining their practical meaning. A communications officer rewrote the opening: a device that reports pressure was sending unreliable readings, and engineers were checking the supply using independent measurements. No interruption had been detected, but the investigation was continuing.

The officer removed unnecessary technical detail while retaining the distinction between a faulty reading and a confirmed supply problem. She also avoided changing no interruption had been detected into there is no risk. The shorter wording would have been more reassuring, but it would have overstated what the checks established.

The internal note kept the technical terms because engineers needed precision to continue the work. The public notice included a time for the next update and a contact route for residents reporting an actual loss of supply. Neither audience received a childish or evasive version.

Adapting register involved selecting the explanation relevant to each recipient, not changing the underlying facts. Plain language succeeded when readers could understand both the current finding and its limits, then decide whether any action was necessary. Accessibility and accuracy supported each other rather than competing for space in the message.

passage_questions.answer_en: Selecting audience-relevant explanations while preserving facts and essential uncertainty.

units.passage_en:
Two days before a community exhibition opened, its sponsor asked the designer to add a series of interactive displays. The sponsor described them as small changes and emphasised the importance of a good partnership. The designer wanted to preserve the relationship, but knew that accepting the request would undermine testing of the displays already promised.

Her first draft response was full of hesitant phrases. It suggested that the additions might be rather difficult, although she would see what she could do. A colleague pointed out that the sponsor could reasonably read this as reluctant agreement. Politeness had made the practical boundary ambiguous.

The revised response acknowledged why the new idea appealed to the sponsor. It then stated clearly that the additions could not be completed safely within the existing deadline. The designer offered two counterproposals: replace one planned display with a simpler interactive version, or develop the additional series for a later event under a separate schedule and budget.

She also identified what would remain unchanged: the opening date and the quality checks for the agreed exhibition. Any replacement would be subject to approval by noon the following day. This made the consequences of each choice visible rather than hiding them in a general refusal.

The sponsor chose the smaller replacement. The exchange did not eliminate disappointment, but it prevented scope creep from becoming a broken promise. A diplomatic refusal can protect a relationship precisely because it gives the other person an accurate basis for deciding, rather than temporary reassurance followed by failure.

passage_questions.question_en: Why was the first draft risky?
passage_questions.answer_en: Its hesitation could be interpreted as agreement to do the extra work.

passage_questions.answer_en: Two days.

passage_questions.question_en: Which option did the sponsor choose?
passage_questions.answer_en: The smaller replacement of one planned display.

passage_questions.question_he: למה מתייחס them במשפט hiding them in a general refusal?
passage_questions.question_en: What does them refer to in hiding them in a general refusal?
passage_questions.answer_en: The consequences of each choice.

passage_questions.question_he: איך סירוב יכול להגן על היחסים?
passage_questions.question_en: How can refusal protect the relationship?
passage_questions.answer_en: It provides accurate expectations and prevents an unfulfillable promise.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה תנאי עצר התלבטות ללא סוף?
passage_questions.question_en: Which condition prevented indefinite indecision?
passage_questions.answer_en: Approval of any replacement by noon the following day.

units.passage_en:
A community arts programme required applicants to upload a short video before midnight on Friday. The organisers argued that the same deadline and format for everyone made selection fair. When several applicants missed it, the committee initially rejected requests for exceptions as inconsistent treatment.

An adviser asked what the video requirement was meant to establish. The committee wanted evidence of motivation and a basic idea for a project; it was not assessing filming skills. Some applicants had limited access to suitable devices, while others relied on a support worker whose appointments were available only during office hours. A uniform procedure was therefore creating obstacles unrelated to the intended criteria.

Removing all deadlines was not practical because places and funding were limited. The committee instead allowed an audio recording or a short supported telephone application. A clearly defined extension could be requested when an access barrier prevented submission. The public guidance explained eligibility and required the committee to record reasons for its decisions.

This did not guarantee that every applicant would receive a place. It preserved selection on the stated criteria while reducing unintended exclusion. The committee also reviewed whether the alternatives were being communicated early enough, since an exception is of little use to someone who never learns it exists.

The debate showed that consistency and equity need not be opposites. A justified variation can be more faithful to a programme's purpose than an identical procedure, provided that the variation is transparent, proportionate and open to review rather than dependent on personal favour.

passage_questions.question_en: Why was the application procedure changed?
passage_questions.answer_en: It created access barriers unrelated to motivation and project ideas.

passage_questions.question_en: What was not being assessed through the video?
passage_questions.answer_en: Filming skills.

passage_questions.question_en: Which two alternatives were offered?
passage_questions.answer_en: An audio recording or supported telephone application.

passage_questions.question_he: למה מתייחס the variation בפסקה האחרונה?
passage_questions.question_en: What does the variation refer to in the final paragraph?
passage_questions.answer_en: Justified alternative procedures or extensions addressing access barriers.

passage_questions.question_he: למה פרסום החריג חשוב כמו עצם קיומו?
passage_questions.question_en: Why does communicating the exception matter?
passage_questions.answer_en: People cannot use an accommodation they do not know exists.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה מנגנון בטקסט מגן מפני העדפה אישית?
passage_questions.question_en: Which safeguard reduces personal favour?
passage_questions.answer_en: Transparent eligibility and recorded reasons open to review.

units.passage_en:
A delivery cooperative reported that customer complaints had doubled, from twenty in June to forty in July. One director described this as evidence that service quality had deteriorated dramatically. Another claimed the opposite after noticing that deliveries had risen from one thousand to three thousand over the same period.

Both directors had selected a real figure, but neither had yet provided a sufficient account. The absolute number of complaints had increased, creating more work for the support team. The complaint rate had fallen from two percent of deliveries to roughly one point three percent. That relative improvement did not make the additional unhappy customers disappear.

A breakdown revealed a further complication. Most new deliveries were small local orders with few reported problems. Complaints about large regional orders had increased both in number and as a proportion of those orders. The aggregate rate was therefore concealing a group whose experience had worsened.

The cooperative also changed its reporting form in July, making complaints easier to submit. Some of the observed increase might reflect improved reporting rather than a new operational fault. The available data could not establish the size of that effect.

The final review separated workload, overall complaint rate and subgroup experience. It proposed examining severity and following the same measures over several months. A robust interpretation required the denominator, the distribution and the measurement process. None of those replaced the headline figures; together, they explained why a single apparently decisive number could support several incomplete stories about the service.

passage_questions.question_en: What does the aggregate rate conceal?
passage_questions.answer_en: A worsening experience for large regional orders.

passage_questions.question_en: How many deliveries occurred in July?
passage_questions.answer_en: Three thousand.

passage_questions.question_en: What changed in the reporting form?
passage_questions.answer_en: It became easier to submit complaints.

passage_questions.question_he: למה מתייחס that effect בפסקה הרביעית?
passage_questions.question_en: What does that effect refer to in paragraph four?
passage_questions.answer_en: The effect of easier reporting on the number of recorded complaints.

passage_questions.question_he: איך שתי הטענות הראשוניות יכולות להיות חלקיות?
passage_questions.question_en: How could both initial claims be incomplete?
passage_questions.answer_en: One ignored delivery volume; the other ignored workload, subgroups and reporting changes.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה נתון חסר כדי לחשב שיעור לקבוצה האזורית?
passage_questions.question_en: What missing figure is needed for the regional subgroup rate?
passage_questions.answer_en: The number of large regional orders in each month.

units.passage_en:
A town museum planned an exhibition about a factory that had closed thirty years earlier. Many residents remembered it as a source of secure work and close friendships. The curator expected a largely celebratory display until interviews revealed a more complicated collective memory.

One former supervisor described generous opportunities for promotion. A worker who had spent years on temporary contracts remembered uncertainty and unequal treatment. Their testimony did not necessarily contradict the same factual claim. They had occupied different positions, at different times, and had access to different opportunities within the institution.

The archive helped establish some boundaries. Employment records showed that permanent jobs had become less common during the factory's final decade. They could corroborate the change in contracts, but not determine how every employee had felt. Photographs of social events demonstrated that activities occurred; they did not establish that everyone felt included.

The curator arranged the exhibition around questions rather than a single emotional conclusion. Labels identified who was speaking and when they had worked there. A timeline distinguished documented changes from personal recollections. Visitors were invited to contribute missing perspectives, including those of cleaners and delivery workers who had previously been overlooked.

The resulting display still commemorated the factory's importance, but resisted presenting nostalgia as a complete history. It also avoided dismissing warm memories simply because hardship existed alongside them. In retrospect, residents could recognise a shared institution without being required to share an identical experience of it. A nuanced public account emerged through careful attribution, comparison and acknowledgement of gaps, rather than selecting whichever testimony produced the most attractive story.

passage_questions.question_en: How did the exhibition avoid a one-sided story?
passage_questions.answer_en: It attributed different memories and separated documented changes from recollections.

passage_questions.question_en: What did employment records show?
passage_questions.answer_en: Permanent jobs became less common in the final decade.

passage_questions.question_en: Which workers' perspectives had been overlooked?
passage_questions.answer_en: Cleaners and delivery workers.

passage_questions.question_en: What does They refer to in paragraph three?
passage_questions.answer_en: Employment records.

passage_questions.question_he: למה תמונת אירוע אינה מוכיחה תחושת שייכות?
passage_questions.question_en: Why does an event photograph not prove inclusion?

passage_questions.question_en: Which contextual detail should accompany testimony?

This would not cancel anyone's memories; it would help visitors understand why genuine recollections can differ within a shared history.

units.passage_en:
Two local websites reported the same overnight bridge closure. One headline celebrated engineers who had prevented a dangerous failure. The other accused officials of leaving commuters stranded. Neither headline was invented, yet each directed attention towards a different part of the event.

The first article foregrounded the discovery of a damaged support and quoted the inspection team. It explained that closing the bridge immediately had reduced the risk of collapse. Travel disruption appeared only near the end. The second article opened with interviews with workers who had missed shifts and parents who could not reach childcare. The engineering explanation was included, but briefly and without detail.

A media class compared the pieces. Students identified loaded language, the order of information and whose voices were treated as authoritative. They also noticed missing context. Neither article stated when alternative routes had been announced or whether emergency transport had been available. These omissions made it harder to assess the quality of the response, even though the need for closure was not seriously disputed.

The teacher cautioned against treating every editorial choice as proof of dishonesty. A short report must select, and audiences may reasonably care about different consequences. The relevant question was whether those choices produced a materially misleading understanding.

For their own summary, students retained both the safety reason and the disruption. They attributed criticisms rather than presenting them as established fact, then identified the information still needed. Their account was not impartial because it lacked emphasis. It was more defensible because its emphasis remained proportionate to the evidence and left room for consequences the original headlines had backgrounded.

passage_questions.question_en: What is the main difference between the reports?
passage_questions.answer_en: One foregrounded safety prevention; the other foregrounded disruption to commuters.

passage_questions.question_en: What did the engineers discover?
passage_questions.answer_en: A damaged bridge support.

passage_questions.question_en: Which information was missing from both reports?
passage_questions.answer_en: When alternatives were announced and whether emergency transport was available.

passage_questions.question_he: למי מתייחס They במשפט They attributed criticisms?
passage_questions.question_en: Who does They refer to in They attributed criticisms?
passage_questions.answer_en: The students writing their own summary.

passage_questions.question_he: למה בחירה עריכתית אינה כשלעצמה הוכחת שקר?
passage_questions.question_en: Why is selection alone not proof of dishonesty?
passage_questions.answer_en: Short reports must select information and audiences may reasonably prioritise different effects.

passage_questions.question_he: איך הסיכום הבחין בין ביקורת לעובדה?
passage_questions.question_en: How did the summary distinguish criticism from fact?
passage_questions.answer_en: It attributed criticisms to their speakers.

Both consequences matter, but neither report establishes whether alternative transport was communicated promptly. I would retain the engineering explanation and attribute residents' criticisms clearly. Without evidence about the response, it would be premature either to praise the entire operation or to portray the closure itself as unnecessary.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: One neighbour demands silence; the other refuses restrictions. Where do you start?

dialogue.text_en: I would clarify the specific needs behind those entrenched positions.

dialogue.speaker: teacher

dialogue.text_en: I can recognise lost sleep without endorsing every accusation.

dialogue.text_en: Use the named contact and review the specific evidence at the agreed point.

units.passage_en:
A rehearsal room occupied the ground floor of an apartment building. Musicians argued that they had permission to use it until ten. Residents above it demanded an end to amplified rehearsals. After several tense messages, each side described the other as unreasonable, and discussion centred on who had the stronger right to win.

A volunteer mediator asked for accounts of particular incidents. One resident worked early shifts and needed sleep before nine. Another was disturbed less by music than by equipment being dragged through the hallway. The musicians needed access after work and could not afford a commercial studio. Their underlying interests were more specific than the original demands suggested.

The mediator acknowledged the residents' disrupted evenings without assuming every complaint had the same cause. She also recognised the musicians' need for a viable practice space. Acknowledgement did not require deciding that either group's interpretation was entirely correct.

The proposed arrangement ended amplified playing at eight thirty on work nights and allowed later acoustic practice. Equipment would be moved on padded trolleys, and a monthly schedule would identify occasional weekend sessions in advance. Residents agreed to report a specific time and type of disturbance instead of sending accusations to the entire building.

A four-week review and a named contact created a contingency if the changes failed. Neither side received complete victory, but both retained something essential. By separating positions from interests, the discussion became a search for workable conditions rather than a contest over whose experience counted. The agreement remained provisional, because practical effects would matter more than how conciliatory the final meeting sounded.

passage_questions.question_en: What allowed mediation to progress?
passage_questions.answer_en: Identifying specific interests and disturbances behind broad opposing demands.

passage_questions.question_he: מתי תסתיים נגינה מוגברת בערבי עבודה?
passage_questions.question_en: When would amplified playing end on work nights?
passage_questions.answer_en: At eight thirty.

passage_questions.question_en: How would equipment be moved?
passage_questions.answer_en: On padded trolleys.

passage_questions.question_he: למי מתייחס both במשפט both retained something essential?
passage_questions.question_en: Who are both in both retained something essential?
passage_questions.answer_en: The residents and the musicians.

passage_questions.question_en: Why did the agreement remain provisional?
passage_questions.answer_en: Its practical effects needed review rather than assuming a good meeting guaranteed success.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה שינוי מפריד בין תלונה להאשמה כללית?
passage_questions.question_en: Which change makes complaints more specific?
passage_questions.answer_en: Reporting the time and type of disturbance to a named contact.

units.roleplay_prompt_he: תווכו בין שכנים למוזיקאים. נסחו צורך של כל צד, הכירו בחוויה בלי לפסוק עובדות, והציעו הסדר עם מדד ובדיקה.
units.model_response_en: What I am hearing is that residents need predictable quiet before early shifts, while the musicians need an affordable evening practice space. Those needs are difficult but not necessarily incompatible. Could amplified rehearsals finish earlier, with acoustic practice afterwards? We should also address equipment noise separately. A named contact and a short review period would let both sides report specific effects without returning immediately to accusations or demands for total victory.
units.writing_prompt_he: כתבו הצעת גישור בת 230–280 מילים: עמדות וצרכים, שתי הכרות, ויתורים הדדיים, חריג ומנגנון בדיקה.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: Would you choose the higher salary automatically?

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: How could you keep options open?
dialogue.text_he: איך אפשר להשאיר אפשרויות פתוחות?

dialogue.speaker: model

dialogue.text_he: האם בדיקת שכר מבטיחה העלאה?

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: No. It commits the employer to a review, not a predetermined outcome.
dialogue.text_he: לא. היא מחייבת בדיקה, ולא תוצאה שנקבעה מראש.

units.passage_en:
After several years in the same job, Lior received two offers. A large firm promised a substantial salary increase and a clear promotion structure. A small organisation offered less money but greater autonomy and work closely aligned with his interests. Friends quickly divided into those advising him to follow his passion and those warning him never to sacrifice stability.

Lior found both slogans unhelpful. He supported a family member and could not ignore predictable expenses. Equally, a salary figure did not describe the hours, commuting demands or kind of experience he would gain. He listed the opportunity costs of each option: accepting one meant giving up benefits that the other might provide.

He then sought information that could change the decision. The larger firm clarified that its advertised flexibility did not apply during the first six months. The smaller organisation explained its funding period and agreed to a salary review after a year, without promising an increase it could not guarantee. Both conversations narrowed uncertainty without removing it.

On reflection, Lior chose the larger firm, but negotiated a defined training pathway and a discussion about flexible hours after the initial period. He also set a personal review date rather than treating the move as his final professional identity.

The decision was not proof that security always outweighs autonomy. It reflected his present constraints and the evidence available. Evaluating a career trajectory required distinguishing an attractive story about the future from specific commitments, and recognising that a sensible choice can remain revisable when circumstances or priorities change.

passage_questions.question_he: למה שתי העצות הכלליות לא הספיקו?
passage_questions.question_en: Why were the two general slogans insufficient?
passage_questions.answer_en: They ignored Lior's specific constraints, work conditions and competing benefits.

passage_questions.question_he: כמה זמן הוגבלה הגמישות בחברה הגדולה?
passage_questions.question_en: How long was flexibility restricted at the larger firm?
passage_questions.answer_en: The first six months.

passage_questions.question_he: מה התחייב הארגון הקטן לעשות אחרי שנה?
passage_questions.question_en: What did the small organisation commit to after a year?
passage_questions.answer_en: A salary review, without guaranteeing an increase.

passage_questions.question_he: למה מתייחס it במשפט it reflected his present constraints?
passage_questions.question_en: What does it refer to in It reflected his present constraints?
passage_questions.answer_en: Lior's decision.

passage_questions.question_en: Why did he set a personal review date?
passage_questions.answer_en: To reassess a revisable choice as circumstances or priorities changed.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה הבדל בטקסט יש בין ציפייה להתחייבות?
passage_questions.question_en: Which distinction separates expectation from commitment?
passage_questions.answer_en: A promised salary review is not a promised salary increase.

units.roleplay_prompt_he: ייעצו לאדם עם שתי הצעות עבודה. בררו אילוץ וערך, הבחינו בין הבטחה להערכה ונסחו המלצה מותנית הניתנת לבדיקה.
units.model_response_en: I would not frame this as a simple choice between money and fulfilment. Your current responsibilities make stability relevant, while autonomy and transferable skills affect your longer-term trajectory. Before deciding, I would ask both employers for specific commitments about hours, training and review points. The better option is the one that fits your present constraints while leaving room to reassess, rather than the one with the most attractive slogan.
units.writing_prompt_he: כתבו המלצה בת 230–280 מילים: שתי חלופות, עלות חלופית לכל אחת, מידע שמשנה החלטה, המלצה מותנית ומועד בדיקה.

language_focus.rule_he: בתנאי מעורב אפשר לקשר בחירה שלא התרחשה בעבר לתוצאה מדומיינת בהווה. תנאי העבר נבנה ב־if had ובצורת past participle. תוצאת ההווה נבנית ב־would ובפועל בסיס, ולעיתים now מבהירה את הזמן. אין להוסיף have רק מפני שפסוקית התנאי מתייחסת לעבר.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: The team closes more cases. Has the service improved?
dialogue.text_he: הצוות סוגר יותר תיקים. האם השירות השתפר?

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: Only if closure is a reliable proxy for resolution.
dialogue.text_he: רק אם סגירה היא מדד עקיף אמין לפתרון.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: Some customers reopen the same issue repeatedly.
dialogue.text_he: חלק מהלקוחות פותחים שוב ושוב אותה בעיה.

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: Then the incentive structure may reward speed over quality.
dialogue.text_he: אז מבנה התמריצים עשוי לתגמל מהירות על פני איכות.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: What would a more holistic review include?
dialogue.text_he: מה תכלול בדיקה מקיפה יותר?

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: Repeat contacts, actual resolution and qualitative customer accounts.
dialogue.text_he: פניות חוזרות, פתרון ממשי ותיאורי לקוחות איכותניים.

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.text_en: Why keep response time at all?
dialogue.text_he: למה בכלל לשמור את מדד זמן התגובה?

dialogue.speaker: model
dialogue.text_en: Prompt help still matters; it should complement evidence of resolution.
dialogue.text_he: סיוע מהיר עדיין חשוב; הוא צריך להשלים ראיות לפתרון.

units.passage_en:
A repair service introduced a target for closing customer cases within one day. Managers wanted customers to receive faster help, and the number of cases marked closed rose sharply. At the monthly meeting, the dashboard appeared to show a clear success.

Technicians described a different experience. Straightforward problems were handled quickly, but complex cases sometimes required a second visit or a part from another supplier. Staff felt pressure to close these cases after the first contact and ask customers to open a new request if the problem continued. The measure rewarded an administrative event rather than the underlying objective of a completed repair.

No manager had instructed staff to mislead customers. Nevertheless, the incentive structure made an unhelpful response easier to justify. Reopened requests were counted as new cases, so the dashboard did not connect them to unresolved work. The faster the team appeared to perform, the less visible that continuing work became.

The revised system retained response time as one measure, but added successful resolution, repeat contact and a small sample of customer accounts. Complex cases could remain open with a clear explanation and next action. Managers also checked whether technicians had enough authority and resources to resolve recurring faults.

The change did not make every measure perfect. Customer comments could be selective, and accurate linking of cases required effort. However, several imperfect sources together gave a more useful picture than one easily optimised number. The episode illustrated how a proxy can become a target in its own right, and why performance review should keep returning to the purpose the metric was meant to serve.

passage_questions.question_en: What was the central problem with the measure?
passage_questions.answer_en: It rewarded administrative closure rather than completed repair.

passage_questions.question_en: How were reopened requests counted?
passage_questions.answer_en: As new cases.

passage_questions.question_en: What qualitative evidence was added?
passage_questions.answer_en: A small sample of customer accounts.

passage_questions.question_en: What does them refer to in paragraph three?
passage_questions.answer_en: Reopened requests.

passage_questions.question_he: למה אין צורך בהוראת הטעיה כדי שייווצר עיוות?
passage_questions.question_en: Why was an instruction to mislead unnecessary?
passage_questions.answer_en: The incentives already made premature closure advantageous.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה תנאי איפשר להשאיר תיק מורכב פתוח?
passage_questions.question_en: What condition allowed a complex case to remain open?
passage_questions.answer_en: A clear explanation and next action.

units.roleplay_prompt_he: המורה משבח צוות שסוגר פניות במהירות. בקשו מידע נוסף, הסבירו מנגנון תמריץ והציעו שני מדדים משלימים והגנה על מקרים מורכבים.
units.model_response_en: Faster closure is encouraging only if it reflects actual resolution. If repeat requests are counted separately, the dashboard may conceal unfinished repairs and reward premature closure. I would retain response time but link related cases, examine repeat contact and sample customers' accounts. Complex cases should remain open with a clear next action. That would align the incentive structure more closely with successful repairs, rather than administrative appearance.
units.writing_prompt_he: כתבו ביקורת מדידה בת 230–280 מילים: מטרה, מדד עקיף, שרשרת תמריצים, תוצאה לא מכוונת ושיטת הערכה מאוזנת.

language_focus.rule_he: תנאי עם if בהווה ותוצאה עם may מציג מנגנון אפשרי. הוא מתאים לתיאור סיכון שהתמריץ עלול ליצור, בלי לקבוע שכבר נצפה אצל כולם. אפשר לפרט את השרשרת באמצעות פעולה ולאחריה תוצאה לא רצויה. הטענה הסיבתית עדיין דורשת ראיות כשמדובר בניתוח מציאותי.
language_focus.example_en: If managers reward only speed, staff may close cases before repairs are finished.
language_focus.contrast_en: Rewarding speed alone can encourage premature closure.
language_focus.prompt_he: נסחו סיכון אפשרי: אם מנהלים מתגמלים רק מהירות, עובדים עלולים לסגור פניות לפני שהתיקונים הושלמו. השתמשו ב־If וב־may.

units.passage_en:
A language workshop advertised a final chance to enrol, supported by enthusiastic testimonials and a countdown timer. When potential participants returned the next morning, the timer had restarted. The organiser argued that urgency encouraged people to stop postponing a decision they would eventually appreciate.

A colleague questioned that justification. Encouraging action could be helpful, but a fabricated deadline deprived people of accurate information. Some applicants were comparing childcare arrangements or checking whether the fee fitted their budget. Their hesitation was not necessarily a lack of motivation to be overcome.

The team reviewed the campaign. A genuine deadline existed because small groups had to be arranged before the first session. They replaced the repeating timer with that date and explained its purpose. Testimonials remained, but were identified as individual experiences rather than proof of typical progress. The description also stated the expected weekly commitment and the procedure for withdrawing before the workshop began.

The revised message still used persuasion. It explained the benefits, gave concrete examples of activities and invited applicants to choose a suitable group. It simply avoided treating uncertainty or financial pressure as weaknesses to exploit. Staff could answer questions without being instructed to turn every enquiry into an immediate payment.

The organiser worried that fewer people might register instantly. The colleague proposed measuring not only initial sign-ups, but also informed participation, early withdrawals and complaints about expectations. A credible campaign would be judged by whether it attracted participants who understood the commitment, rather than by how efficiently it converted a moment of anxiety into a purchase.

passage_questions.question_en: What distinguishes the revised campaign?
passage_questions.answer_en: It used a genuine deadline and contextualised benefits and commitments.

passage_questions.question_en: What happened to the timer the next morning?
passage_questions.answer_en: It restarted.

passage_questions.question_he: למה באמת היה צריך מועד הרשמה?
passage_questions.question_en: Why was a real deadline needed?
passage_questions.answer_en: Small groups had to be arranged before the first session.

passage_questions.question_en: Whose hesitation is described by Their hesitation?
passage_questions.answer_en: Applicants checking childcare or budget constraints.

passage_questions.question_he: למה הרשמות מיידיות אינן מדד הצלחה מספיק?
passage_questions.question_en: Why are immediate sign-ups an insufficient success measure?
passage_questions.answer_en: They may result from pressure and lead to withdrawals or unmet expectations.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה מדד נוסף מהטקסט בודק הבנת התחייבות?
passage_questions.question_en: Which further measure checks expectation quality?
passage_questions.answer_en: Early withdrawals or complaints about expectations.

units.passage_en:
A freelance photographer and a community organisation agreed by email to produce images for a new website. Their summary promised regular updates, prompt delivery and reasonable efforts to include every volunteer. Both sides felt reassured because the phrases sounded cooperative. Difficulties emerged when they tried to decide whether the work had been completed.

The organiser expected edited photographs of every volunteer within one week. The photographer understood prompt delivery as sending a first selection within a week of the final session. Several volunteers had not attended that session, and no additional visit had been included in the quoted price. Neither interpretation required bad faith; the scope of work had simply remained ambiguous.

Before proceeding, they rewrote the practical plan. It identified the number of edited images, the delivery date, the file formats and one included revision round. Updates would be sent on Tuesdays by email. The organisation would provide a confirmed attendance list and obtain any permissions it was responsible for arranging. Missing volunteers would be recorded, and an additional session would require a mutually agreed change to timing and cost.

They also clarified what counted as acceptance: the organiser would check technical requirements and notify the photographer of specific issues within a defined period. This discussion did not establish the legal effect of every earlier phrase. It gave both parties a clearer shared basis for action and for seeking professional advice if a significant dispute remained.

The lesson was linguistic as well as practical: friendly wording can conceal different expectations, and clarity often depends on naming the event from which a deadline is measured.

passage_questions.question_en: What caused the initial disagreement?
passage_questions.answer_en: Cooperative but ambiguous phrases concealed different expectations about scope and timing.

passage_questions.question_en: On which day would updates be sent?
passage_questions.answer_en: Tuesdays.

passage_questions.question_en: How many revision rounds were included?
passage_questions.answer_en: One.

passage_questions.question_he: למי מתייחס they במשפט they rewrote the practical plan?
passage_questions.question_en: Who does they refer to in they rewrote the practical plan?
passage_questions.answer_en: The photographer and the organiser.

passage_questions.question_he: למה חשוב לציין מאיזה אירוע נמדד שבוע?
passage_questions.question_en: Why specify the event from which a week is measured?
passage_questions.answer_en: Different starting events can produce different expected deadlines.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה שינוי מצריך הסכמה נוספת לפי התוכנית?
passage_questions.question_en: Which change requires further agreement?
passage_questions.answer_en: An additional session for missing volunteers, including time and cost.

I suggest naming the final number of edited images, the date measured from the last agreed session, and the included revision round. We should also record which attendance and permission arrangements depend on the organisation. That would not settle every legal question, but it would give both parties a clearer practical basis for identifying completion or requesting a change.

dialogue.text_en: No. Selection and self-justification can distort a largely factual story.
dialogue.text_he: לא. בחירה והצדקה עצמית יכולות לעוות סיפור שעיקרו עובדתי.

units.passage_en:
For years, I told the story of leaving our neighbourhood choir as though I had been pushed out. I described the conductor's strictness, the inconvenient rehearsals and the concert programme I disliked. Friends usually agreed that I had been treated unfairly. Their sympathy made the account easier to repeat.

Recently, I found an old exchange of messages. The conductor had offered to discuss my concerns after rehearsal. I had replied that there was nothing to discuss. Another member had suggested sharing transport, an offer I barely remembered. Neither message proved that the choir had been an ideal place. They did complicate my claim that no reasonable alternative had existed.

I had also left out my own ambition. A smaller group had offered me a solo, and I was excited by the attention. Admitting this would have weakened the image of a reluctant departure. Without deliberately inventing events, I had selected the ones that made me appear entirely justified.

When an old friend asked about the choir last week, I tried a different version. I still described the difficulties, but acknowledged that I had rejected a conversation and been attracted by another opportunity. The revised account felt less tidy and, unexpectedly, more comfortable.

I cannot recover every feeling I had at the time, and hindsight may create its own distortions. Yet I can distinguish between remembering a grievance and proving that I bore no responsibility. The story now leaves room for motives that coexist, rather than requiring one person to have been wholly right and another wholly wrong.

passage_questions.question_en: How did the narrator's account change?
passage_questions.answer_en: It acknowledged rejected alternatives and personal ambition alongside genuine difficulties.

passage_questions.question_en: What did another choir member offer?
passage_questions.answer_en: Shared transport.

passage_questions.question_he: מה משך את המספר לקבוצה הקטנה?
passage_questions.question_en: What attracted the narrator to the smaller group?
passage_questions.answer_en: An offered solo and the associated attention.

passage_questions.question_he: למה מתייחס They בתחילת משפט They did complicate?
passage_questions.question_en: What does They refer to in They did complicate?
passage_questions.answer_en: The rediscovered messages.

passage_questions.question_he: למה אהדת החברים חיזקה גרסה חלקית?
passage_questions.question_en: Why did friends' sympathy reinforce the partial account?
passage_questions.answer_en: It rewarded repeating a version in which the narrator seemed entirely wronged.

passage_questions.question_he: איזה משפט מתוקן ישמור גם על קושי וגם על אחריות?
passage_questions.question_en: What revised statement preserves difficulty and responsibility?
passage_questions.answer_en: The rehearsals were difficult, but I rejected discussion and wanted the solo elsewhere.

I would ask what conversations were offered and whether another opportunity influenced your decision. A more balanced account could acknowledge both the pressure you felt and the choices you made. That need not become self-condemnation; it simply leaves room for mixed motives and shared responsibility rather than a perfectly tidy explanation.

dialogue.speaker: model

dialogue.text_he: פרשנות סבירה צריכה ראיות מהסצנה כולה.

dialogue.text_en: Could it symbolise both protection and exclusion?

units.passage_en:
In a short film shown at a community festival, an elderly woman repeatedly repairs a door at the entrance to her house. Neighbours offer to replace it, but she refuses. In the final scene, she locks the restored door, then leaves through an open gate in the garden. The film provides no explanation in dialogue.

During the discussion, one viewer called the door a symbol of resistance to change. The interpretation fitted the woman's refusal of a replacement, but another viewer noted that it did not fully explain her calm departure. If she were simply afraid of the outside world, why would the final image show her walking towards it?

A third viewer connected the repairs to continuity rather than fear. The door might preserve a link with the house's history, while the gate allowed a new direction. This reading drew support from an earlier scene in which the woman touched marks recording children's heights. However, the viewer acknowledged that the film did not identify whose children they had been.

The director, present at the discussion, declined to announce a single correct meaning. She explained one production choice: the sound of the lock had been made unusually loud. That detail could evoke security, finality or exclusion, depending on how it was connected with the rest of the film.

The strongest contributions did not treat an open-ended work as permission to say anything. They used specific images, considered counterevidence and distinguished cultural associations from facts supplied by the film. Interpretation remained contestable, but it was not arbitrary. The conversation deepened when disagreement made previously unnoticed details salient.

units.passage_en:
A town proposed converting its central square into a largely car-free public space. Supporters argued that quieter streets would make the centre more pleasant and allow markets and outdoor events. Opponents were often portrayed as people who simply disliked change. That characterisation made the debate easier to win rhetorically and harder to resolve practically.

At a public discussion, a resident presented the strongest objection instead. Some people could not walk far, deliveries were essential to shops, and nearby streets might receive displaced traffic. A successful square would not justify creating unacceptable barriers elsewhere. These were pragmatic concerns about implementation, rather than a principled claim that cars should always have priority.

Supporters conceded that excluding ordinary traffic was not sufficient to create an accessible public space. They proposed designated access times, nearby drop-off points and monitoring on surrounding streets. Opponents then asked whether those arrangements would be reliable in practice, especially during events. The discussion shifted from competing slogans to conditions the proposal would have to meet.

The town agreed to a limited trial, but with criteria published before it began. Evidence would include pedestrian use, delivery difficulties, access complaints and traffic changes outside the square. The review would not count a crowded opening celebration as conclusive success or a single difficult morning as conclusive failure.

A coherent position could therefore remain supportive while contingent. The trial's burden was to demonstrate that benefits could be achieved without avoidable exclusion. Stating what would change one's mind did not weaken the argument. It showed that the conclusion depended on reasons, rather than loyalty to a preferred outcome regardless of what happened.

passage_questions.question_en: What improved the quality of the debate?
passage_questions.answer_en: Presenting the strongest practical objections and specifying conditions for success.

passage_questions.question_en: Which change would be monitored outside the square?
passage_questions.answer_en: Traffic on surrounding streets.

passage_questions.question_en: When were trial criteria to be published?
passage_questions.answer_en: Before the trial began.

passage_questions.question_en: What does These refer to in paragraph two?
passage_questions.answer_en: Concerns about walking access, deliveries and displaced traffic.

passage_questions.question_he: למה חגיגת פתיחה צפופה אינה מספיקה?
passage_questions.question_en: Why is a crowded opening celebration insufficient?

passage_questions.question_he: איזה ממצא מהטקסט יכול לשנות תמיכה?
passage_questions.question_en: Which finding could reasonably change support?

units.passage_en:
When Tom arrived twelve minutes late for a rehearsal, his friend said, Perfect timing. Everyone has been waiting to begin. Tom recognised the ironic compliment from the tone and apologised. The remark carried criticism, but their established rapport made it possible to acknowledge the problem without a prolonged argument.

A week later, a new member received a message containing only the same two opening words. Her bus had been delayed, and she was already anxious about joining the group. She read the phrase literally at first, then wondered whether it was sarcastic. Without vocal cues or a clear description of the situation, she could not confidently infer the sender's intention.

Instead of replying with an accusation, she wrote that she was sorry for the delay and asked whether the group had missed an important part of the rehearsal. The organiser clarified that she had arrived just as the earlier session ended; the message had been genuinely positive. He added that he understood how the wording could have sounded different.

The comparison illustrates why pragmatic competence is more than memorising that certain expressions are ironic. Meaning depends on circumstances, prosody, relationships and what follows the phrase. Even a skilled listener may need to withhold judgement when those cues are absent.

A charitable interpretation is not an obligation to ignore persistent hostility. It is a practical starting point when the evidence is ambiguous. In this instance, a specific question repaired uncertainty more effectively than either unquestioning literal acceptance or immediate certainty that offence had been intended.

units.passage_en:
The town library could afford to extend opening hours by six hours a week. Its manager proposed adding an hour to each weekday and Saturday morning. A residents' group preferred two late evenings, arguing that current hours excluded people who worked during the day. The council requested a recommendation that considered both demand and access.

Door counts showed the highest attendance on Saturday mornings and just after school. They provided no direct evidence about late-evening demand because the library had never opened then. A survey of current visitors favoured longer Saturdays, but the residents' group pointed out that the sample excluded many people unable to visit. Its own petition demonstrated interest, though signatures did not establish how frequently people would attend.

Staff raised a separate constraint. Late evenings required two employees for safety, reducing the hours that could be added elsewhere. They also warned that extending opening without time for preparation could weaken existing services. These concerns affected implementation rather than disproving the value of access for working residents.

A provisional recommendation proposed one late evening and a shorter Saturday extension for a twelve-week trial. It specified staff cover, communicated the new hours outside the library and collected attendance, first-time visits, costs and staff feedback. The council would also ask whether new users had previously faced an access barrier.

The recommendation acknowledged that a compromise could underperform both original proposals. Nevertheless, a time-limited, properly publicised trial could address an evidence gap more fairly than assuming either current usage or petition signatures settled the matter. Success criteria and a review date would be published before implementation, including conditions under which the allocation should be revised.

passage_questions.question_en: What was the provisional recommendation designed to test?

units.roleplay_prompt_he: המורה הוא חבר מועצה שמעדיף אחת החלופות. הציגו המלצה, שלבו שלושה מקורות, הכירו במגבלה וענו לשתי התנגדויות תוך שמירת תנאי שינוי.
units.model_response_en: I recommend a twelve-week trial combining one late evening with a shorter Saturday extension. Current visitor counts establish existing patterns, but cannot reveal demand when the building has always been closed. The petition identifies interest without proving regular attendance. We should therefore publicise the trial beyond current users, protect staffing requirements and evaluate access as well as total visits. I would revise the allocation if costs or limited new access undermine its justification.
units.writing_prompt_he: כתבו המלצה בת 260–320 מילים למועצה, ולאחריה הודעה לציבור בת 80–100 מילים: מקורות, חלופות, אילוץ, יישום, מדדים ותנאי שינוי. השלימו דיון בעל פה.

language_focus.rule_he: I would recommend מציגה המלצה בשיקול דעת ולא הבטחה לתוצאה. provided that מציבה תנאי להמלצה. אחריה מציינים תנאי שאפשר לבדוק, ולא ניסוח עמום של הצלחה כללית. בפרויקט מסכם אפשר להוסיף בהמשך באילו ממצאים תשתנה ההמלצה.
language_focus.example_en: I would recommend a twelve-week trial, provided that staffing needs are reviewed.
language_focus.contrast_en: I recommend a permanent extension now.
language_focus.prompt_he: המליצו על ניסיון של שנים עשר שבועות בתנאי שייבדקו צורכי כוח האדם. השתמשו ב־I would recommend וב־provided that.
language_focus.answer_en: I would recommend a twelve-week trial, provided that staffing needs are reviewed.
language_focus.feedback_he: ההמלצה מוגבלת בזמן ומותנית בבדיקת כוח האדם. היא אינה המלצה מיידית לשינוי קבוע.

units.input_readiness_he: לפני הטקסט בודקים מה המשתמש כבר מבין. תמיכות חדשות נחלקות לחבילות של עד 6 לפני המפגש או לטקסט קצר יותר. אין להניח שמילת תמיכה כבר ידועה, ואין לדחוס את כל רשימת הגלוסות לדקות המורה. זו קריאה מונחית; קריאה עצמאית דורשת בדיקת כיסוי אישית.
units.prerequisite_he: מיומנות תקשורת מן היחידה הקודמת, או מיון שמראה יכולת מקבילה. קריאה נבדקת בנפרד; אין חסימת שיחה בגלל פענוח.

ביטוי תמיכה לדגם: how many, במשמעות כמה. נלמד להפיק אותו בהמשך; עכשיו אפשר להיעזר בדגם.

postlesson.rubric_he: משמעות מתאימה ליעד + תור קצר שממלא כוונה; במתחיל מותר להיעזר במסגרת הדגם. זו אינה שאלת הבנה של טקסט היחידה שטרם נלמד.
postlesson.hint_he: חזור למשמעות העברית בדגם; שימוש בה הוא תמיכה.
postlesson.feedback_he: בדוק שהכוונה נשמרה. תרגום נכון לבדו אינו מוכיח יכולת הפקה בהקשר.

postlesson.prompt_he: הקשב לפריט המושמע כאשר הכתיב מוסתר. אמור את המשמעות; אם דפוסי הכתב כבר נלמדו, כתוב את מה ששמעת.
postlesson.answer_visibility: author_reviewer_only; audio script must not be visible during learner attempt
postlesson.hint_he: השמע שוב; חשיפת הכתב היא תמיכה. לפני קריאה מספקת אפשר לענות בקול או לבחור משמעות.
postlesson.feedback_he: איות, משמעות וזיהוי שמע הם ראיות שונות; כשל באחד אינו מוחק את האחרים.

postlesson.prompt_he: בחנות דמיונית בקשו בין פריט אחד לחמישה תפוחים או כוסות. אשרו את המספר שהמורה חוזר עליו.
postlesson.answer_anchor_en: Three apples, please. Yes, three. Thank you.
postlesson.rubric_he: מילוי הכוונה, מובנות, התאמה למצב, שימוש עצמאי לפחות באחד מיעדי הפגישה. תשובה אחרת נכונה מתקבלת. זו משימה מתורגלת, לא הוכחת העברה לנושא חדש.
postlesson.hint_he: בחר משפט פתיחה מדגם השיחה; לאחר מכן נסה ללא הדגם.
postlesson.feedback_he: בחר נקודת יעד אחת לתיקון והפק שוב. בדיקת העברה נפרדת משתמשת בטופס חדש אחרי שלוש יחידות.

postlesson.prompt_he: תכנן את המשימה הבאה; בשלב הזה כתוב רק פתיחה ושני פרטים, או אמור אותם בקול: כתבו מספר מתאים ליד one/two/three אחרי האזנה. למי שמוכן: I have two pens.
postlesson.rubric_he: מילוי משימה, מסר ברור, סדר מתאים לרמה ודיוק ביעדים שנלמדו; אין תשובה יחידה.
postlesson.answer_anchor_en: Three apples, please. Yes, three. Thank you.
postlesson.anchor_note_he: הדגם ממחיש שפה ומסר; הוא אינו פתרון יחיד או בהכרח תוצר באורך הכתיבה המבוקש.
postlesson.hint_he: תכנן כוונה, שני פרטים וסיום. במתחיל גם משפט אחד או אמירה בעל פה יכולים להיות שלב לימוד.
postlesson.feedback_he: ראשית בדוק שהמסר עובר; בחר עד שתי נקודות לתיקון וכתוב או הקלט גרסה שנייה.

postlesson.prompt_he: תארו למורה את הבוקר והערב שלכם ושאלו מתי הוא אוכל ארוחת צהריים. נסו לקבוע זמן לשיחת תרגול.
postlesson.answer_anchor_en: I get up at seven. I study after breakfast. I eat dinner at seven in the evening. What time do you eat lunch?
postlesson.rubric_he: מילוי הכוונה, מובנות, התאמה למצב, שימוש עצמאי לפחות באחד מיעדי הפגישה. תשובה אחרת נכונה מתקבלת. זו משימה מתורגלת, לא הוכחת העברה לנושא חדש.
postlesson.hint_he: בחר משפט פתיחה מדגם השיחה; לאחר מכן נסה ללא הדגם.

postlesson.hint_he: תכנן כוונה, שני פרטים וסיום. במתחיל גם משפט אחד או אמירה בעל פה יכולים להיות שלב לימוד.

teacher_script.say_he: כעת נקשיב לקטע. נסה לזהות את המצב המרכזי. אפשר לשמוע שוב. במצב קריאה נפתח את הכתב; אם בודקים האזנה עצמאית משאירים תמלול סגור בניסיון הראשון.
teacher_script.text_en: Maya needs a shirt for work. She goes to a small shop with her sister. A white shirt is twenty shekels, and a green shirt is thirty. Maya likes green. She asks for a small size and tries on the green shirt. It is too small. The shop has a big size too. Maya tries it on and says, "This is good." Her sister looks at black shoes, but they are expensive. She does not buy the shoes.

teacher_script.say_he: היום נעבוד על: מוצאים את הדרך בעיר. המטרה היא לשאול היכן מקום ולהבין מסלול קצר. אפשר לבקש הסבר קצר בעברית או לחלק את המפגש.
teacher_script.say_en: We will practise a useful task step by step. You can ask me to repeat or explain. At the end, you will try a new version without the model.

teacher_script.say_he: לפני הדגם, נסה לומר באנגלית שתי כוונות שכבר פגשנו: רחוב; חנות.
teacher_script.note_he: רק אם הפריטים אכן נלמדו קודם; לאחר דילוג בעקבות מיון בוחרים מן הראיות האישיות.

teacher_script.say_he: הקשב: left. במשמעות של היום: שמאלה. אמור את הצורה, ואז הסבר את המשמעות או בחר את המצב שמתאים לה.
teacher_script.say_en: Listen: left. We are learning this expression with a specific meaning. Say it, then explain when you would use it.
teacher_script.note_he: חזרה אחרי דגם היא תרגול נתמך. אם אין עדיין יכולת קריאה, לא דורשים הקלדה.

teacher_script.say_he: הקשב: right. במשמעות של היום: ימינה. אמור את הצורה, ואז הסבר את המשמעות או בחר את המצב שמתאים לה.
teacher_script.say_en: Listen: right. We are learning this expression with a specific meaning. Say it, then explain when you would use it.
teacher_script.note_he: חזרה אחרי דגם היא תרגול נתמך. אם אין עדיין יכולת קריאה, לא דורשים הקלדה.

teacher_script.say_he: הקשב: straight ahead. במשמעות של היום: ישר קדימה. אמור את הצורה, ואז הסבר את המשמעות או בחר את המצב שמתאים לה.
teacher_script.say_en: Listen: straight ahead. We are learning this expression with a specific meaning. Say it, then explain when you would use it.
teacher_script.note_he: חזרה אחרי דגם היא תרגול נתמך. אם אין עדיין יכולת קריאה, לא דורשים הקלדה.

teacher_script.say_he: הקשב: opposite. במשמעות של היום: מול. אמור את הצורה, ואז הסבר את המשמעות או בחר את המצב שמתאים לה.
teacher_script.say_en: Listen: opposite. We are learning this expression with a specific meaning. Say it, then explain when you would use it.

teacher_script.say_he: הקשב: between. במשמעות של היום: בין. אמור את הצורה, ואז הסבר את המשמעות או בחר את המצב שמתאים לה.
teacher_script.say_en: Listen: between. We are learning this expression with a specific meaning. Say it, then explain when you would use it.

teacher_script.say_he: הקשב: near. במשמעות של היום: קרוב ל־. אמור את הצורה, ואז הסבר את המשמעות או בחר את המצב שמתאים לה.
teacher_script.say_en: Listen: near. We are learning this expression with a specific meaning. Say it, then explain when you would use it.
teacher_script.note_he: חזרה אחרי דגם היא תרגול נתמך. אם אין עדיין יכולת קריאה, לא דורשים הקלדה.

teacher_script.say_he: ננסה את תבנית השימוש מהפגישה הקודמת לפני הצגת הדגם. לפי המפה צריך לפנות שמאלה ליד הפארק. תנו את ההוראה באנגלית במשפט אחד.
teacher_script.contrast_en: Turn right at the park.
teacher_script.task_he: לפי המפה צריך לפנות שמאלה ליד הפארק. תנו את ההוראה באנגלית במשפט אחד.
teacher_script.answer_anchor_en: Turn left at the park.
teacher_script.note_he: Turn מבקש פנייה ו־left מציין שמאלה. at the park קובע את נקודת הציון; החלפת left ב־right תשנה את המסלול.

teacher_script.say_he: לפני הדגם נוודא שהמילים הדרושות להבנה מוכרות. נלמד רק את התמיכות החסרות בחבילות קצרות; אם הן רבות, נעצור ונמשיך במפגש נוסף. אפשר להבין בעזרת שמע ותרגום.
support_script_lines_he: הקשב: ahead. כאן נספק את המשמעות: לפנים (בהמשך הדרך). נשתמש במילה כדי להבין את המצב, ולא נספור זאת כשליפה עצמאית.
הקשב: excuse. כאן נספק את המשמעות: לתרץ או לתת סיבה למעשה. נשתמש במילה כדי להבין את המצב, ולא נספור זאת כשליפה עצמאית.
הקשב: far. כאן נספק את המשמעות: רחוק. נשתמש במילה כדי להבין את המצב, ולא נספור זאת כשליפה עצמאית.
הקשב: follow. כאן נספק את המשמעות: לעקוב אחר. נשתמש במילה כדי להבין את המצב, ולא נספור זאת כשליפה עצמאית.
הקשב: map. כאן נספק את המשמעות: מפה. נשתמש במילה כדי להבין את המצב, ולא נספור זאת כשליפה עצמאית.
הקשב: straight. כאן נספק את המשמעות: ישר. נשתמש במילה כדי להבין את המצב, ולא נספור זאת כשליפה עצמאית.
הקשב: turn. כאן נספק את המשמעות: לפנות (כיוון). נשתמש במילה כדי להבין את המצב, ולא נספור זאת כשליפה עצמאית.
teacher_script.note_he: לפני הטקסט בודקים מה המשתמש כבר מבין. תמיכות חדשות נחלקות לחבילות של עד 6 לפני המפגש או לטקסט קצר יותר. אין להניח שמילת תמיכה כבר ידועה, ואין לדחוס את כל רשימת הגלוסות לדקות המורה. זו קריאה מונחית; קריאה עצמאית דורשת בדיקת כיסוי אישית.

teacher_script.say_he: נקשיב לדגם. בפעם הראשונה המטרה היא להבין מי מדבר ומה הוא רוצה. בפעם השנייה תחליף אחד מהדוברים. התרגום נפתח לפי צורך.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text_en: Excuse me. Where is the station?
turns.text_he: סליחה. איפה התחנה?

turns.speaker: model
turns.text_en: Go straight ahead on this street.
turns.text_he: לכו ישר ברחוב הזה.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text_en: Do I turn left at the park?
turns.text_he: האם לפנות שמאלה ליד הפארק?

turns.speaker: model
turns.text_en: No. Turn right at the park.
turns.text_he: לא. פנו ימינה ליד הפארק.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text_en: Is the station near the supermarket?
turns.text_he: האם התחנה קרובה לסופרמרקט?

turns.speaker: model
turns.text_en: Yes. It is opposite the supermarket.
turns.text_he: כן. היא מול הסופרמרקט.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text_en: Thank you. Is it far?
turns.text_he: תודה. האם זה רחוק?

turns.speaker: model
turns.text_en: No. It is near.
turns.text_he: לא. זה קרוב.

teacher_script.say_he: כעת נקשיב לקטע. נסה לזהות את המצב המרכזי. אפשר לשמוע שוב. במצב קריאה נפתח את הכתב; אם בודקים האזנה עצמאית משאירים תמלול סגור בניסיון הראשון.
teacher_script.text_en: Ben is at a school on Green Street. He wants to go to the station. He asks a woman for help. She says, "Go straight ahead. There is a park on your left. Turn right at the park. The station is opposite the supermarket." Ben looks at a small map. The hospital is between the school and a shop. He does not need the hospital. He follows the street to the park and turns right. He sees the station.
teacher_script.note_he: זהו חומר הוראה מוכר, לא unseen לאחר הצגתו.

teacher_script.say_he: מאיפה בן מתחיל?
teacher_script.say_en: Where does Ben start?
teacher_script.answer_anchor_en: At a school on Green Street.
teacher_script.accept_he: יש לקבל פרפרזה נכונה, תשובה קצרה מתאימה ופרטים תומכים מן הטקסט. לא חייבים להעתיק את הדגם.

teacher_script.say_he: לאן בן רוצה ללכת?
teacher_script.say_en: Where does Ben want to go?
teacher_script.answer_anchor_en: To the station.
teacher_script.accept_he: יש לקבל פרפרזה נכונה, תשובה קצרה מתאימה ופרטים תומכים מן הטקסט. לא חייבים להעתיק את הדגם.

teacher_script.say_he: לאיזה כיוון עליו לפנות ליד הפארק?
teacher_script.say_en: Which way does he turn at the park?
teacher_script.answer_anchor_en: Right.
teacher_script.accept_he: יש לקבל פרפרזה נכונה, תשובה קצרה מתאימה ופרטים תומכים מן הטקסט. לא חייבים להעתיק את הדגם.

teacher_script.say_he: נסה את המשימה המוכרת ללא הדגם. זו הפקה עצמאית של חומר מתורגל; בדיקת העברה רחבה תיעשה במשימה נפרדת אחרי שלוש יחידות. המורה ליד בית הספר במפה. הסבירו דרך לפארק ולתחנה בשתי הוראות בכל פעם ושאלו היכן הסופרמרקט.
teacher_script.say_en: Try the practised task without reading the model. Explain your choice or ask for clarification when needed.
teacher_script.model_en: Go straight ahead. Turn right at the park. The station is opposite the supermarket. Where is the shop?
teacher_script.model_visibility_he: תשובת עוגן למורה. אין להקריא לפני הניסיון העצמאי. משימה זו אינה unseen רק מפני שהדגם מוסתר.

teacher_script.say_he: נפתח כעת את משימת הכתיבה. במפגש הזה תכנן כוונה וכתוב משפט פתיחה; את הטיוטה המלאה והעריכה תשלים בזמן נפרד. ציירו שלושה מקומות או השתמשו במפה הנתונה. כתבו 3 הוראות עם מילת מיקום אחת לפחות.
teacher_script.note_he: הכתיבה המלאה אינה נכללת בדקות המורה. לפי אוריינות אפשר לתרגל בקול, אך במבחן כתיבה עצמאי אין להחליף אוטומטית בדיבור.

teacher_script.say_he: נבדוק מה עשית בלי עזרה ומה עדיין צריך תמיכה. בחר ביטוי אחד שתוכל להשתמש בו מחוץ לשיעור. בפעם הבאה ננסה מצב חדש.

branches.correct_he: המשמעות עברה. כעת ננסה להשתמש בזה במצב מעט שונה. אמור את אותה כוונה עם פרט אחר משלך.
branches.partial_he: הבנתי חלק מהכוונה. נתקן נקודה אחת מן היעד שלמדנו. הקשב לדגם הקצר, ואז נסה שוב עם הפרט שלך.
branches.incorrect_he: נבדוק את המשמעות שוב. הנה שתי אפשרויות מן החומר שלמדנו. בחר אחת, הקשב לדגם ונסה להשתמש בו. הניסיון הזה נתמך.
branches.silence_he: אפשר לענות במילה אחת, לבחור בין שתי אפשרויות או לבקש לשמוע שוב. נתחיל בצעד קטן.
branches.asr_uncertain_he: לא שמעתי בבירור. נסה שוב או הקלד. אין בכך קביעה שהתשובה הלשונית שגויה.
branches.unexpected_valid_he: הניסוח שלך מתאים לכוונה. עכשיו ננסה גם את הביטוי המסוים שלמדנו, כדי שאוכל לבדוק אותו.
branches.fade_support_he: הפעם הדגם מוסתר. אותה מטרה, מצב חדש. אפשר לעצור ולבקש עזרה; אסמן אם השתמשנו בתמיכה.

teacher_script.say_he: כעת נקשיב לקטע. נסה לזהות את המצב המרכזי. אפשר לשמוע שוב. במצב קריאה נפתח את הכתב; אם בודקים האזנה עצמאית משאירים תמלול סגור בניסיון הראשון.
teacher_script.text_en: Ben likes music and football. He can sing, but he cannot swim. On Saturday morning, he often plays football with his friends in the park. Maya likes walking. She sometimes walks to the park and watches the game. After football, Ben and Maya go home together. Ben cooks lunch, and Maya helps him. In the afternoon, they listen to music. They do not work at the weekend. They like having time with friends and doing different things together.

lessons.title_he: מה קורה עכשיו? — רכישה ושיחה נתמכת

teacher_script.say_he: היום נעבוד על: מה קורה עכשיו?. המטרה היא לתאר פעולות בתמונה ולהבחין בין עכשיו להרגל. אפשר לבקש הסבר קצר בעברית או לחלק את המפגש.

teacher_script.note_he: רק אם הפריטים אכן נלמדו קודם; לאחר דילוג בעקבות מיון בוחרים מן הראיות האישיות.

teacher_script.say_he: כדי לתאר מה קורה עכשיו משתמשים ב־am/is/are עם פעולה המסתיימת ב־ing. אחרי she נבחר is, ואחרי they נבחר are. להרגל רגיל אומרים למשל She writes every day, בלי is לפני writes.
teacher_script.text_en: She is writing now.
teacher_script.contrast_en: She writes every day.

teacher_script.note_he: They מקבל כאן are והפעולה היא sleeping. They sleep every day מתאר הרגל; אנחנו מבקשים את מה שקורה עכשיו.

teacher_script.say_he: לפני הדגם נוודא שהמילים הדרושות להבנה מוכרות. נלמד רק את התמיכות החסרות בחבילות קצרות; אם הן רבות, נעצור ונמשיך במפגש נוסף. אפשר להבין בעזרת שמע ותרגום.

teacher_script.note_he: לפני הטקסט בודקים מה המשתמש כבר מבין. תמיכות חדשות נחלקות לחבילות של עד 6 לפני המפגש או לטקסט קצר יותר. אין להניח שמילת תמיכה כבר ידועה, ואין לדחוס את כל רשימת הגלוסות לדקות המורה. זו קריאה מונחית; קריאה עצמאית דורשת בדיקת כיסוי אישית.

teacher_script.say_he: היום נעבוד על: מספרים על טיול. המטרה היא לספר אירוע בעבר בסדר ברור ולענות לשאלות המשך. אפשר לבקש הסבר קצר בעברית או לחלק את המפגש.

teacher_script.say_he: לפני הדגם נוודא שהמילים הדרושות להבנה מוכרות. נלמד רק את התמיכות החסרות בחבילות קצרות; אם הן רבות, נעצור ונמשיך במפגש נוסף. אפשר להבין בעזרת שמע ותרגום.

teacher_script.note_he: לפני הטקסט בודקים מה המשתמש כבר מבין. תמיכות חדשות נחלקות לחבילות של עד 6 לפני המפגש או לטקסט קצר יותר. אין להניח שמילת תמיכה כבר ידועה, ואין לדחוס את כל רשימת הגלוסות לדקות המורה. זו קריאה מונחית; קריאה עצמאית דורשת בדיקת כיסוי אישית.

teacher_script.say_he: נקשיב לדגם. בפעם הראשונה המטרה היא להבין מי מדבר ומה הוא רוצה. בפעם השנייה תחליף אחד מהדוברים. התרגום נפתח לפי צורך.

turns.text_he: כן. קניתי ספר לאחותי.

teacher_script.say_he: כעת נקשיב לקטע. נסה לזהות את המצב המרכזי. אפשר לשמוע שוב. במצב קריאה נפתח את הכתב; אם בודקים האזנה עצמאית משאירים תמלול סגור בניסיון הראשון.
teacher_script.text_en: Two days ago, Maya and Ben took a train to a village near the beach. The journey took one hour. First, they walked through the village and saw some old houses. Ben wanted to take pictures, but he forgot his phone. Maya had her phone, so she took the pictures. Later, they found a small cafe next to the beach. Maya bought two sandwiches and some water. They ate outside because the weather was warm. After lunch, they walked on the beach and talked about their families. At four, they went back to the station. Ben could not find his ticket at first. Finally, he found it in his book. They arrived home at six, tired but happy. Maya sent the pictures to Ben that evening.

teacher_script.say_he: כעת נקשיב לקטע. נסה לזהות את המצב המרכזי. אפשר לשמוע שוב. במצב קריאה נפתח את הכתב; אם בודקים האזנה עצמאית משאירים תמלול סגור בניסיון הראשון.
teacher_script.text_en: Next month, Tom and his sister are going to have a short holiday. They are going to travel by train because they do not have a car. They plan to stay in a small hotel for three nights. The hotel is near the beach, but it is not in the city centre. On the first day, they are going to walk by the sea. On the second day, they are going to visit a museum. Tom wants to buy tickets before the trip, so they do not need to wait outside. His sister is going to book the room this week. Tom is going to pack one small suitcase. He needs warm clothes because the evenings can be cold. They are not going to take many things. They want an easy holiday.

teacher_script.say_he: היום נעבוד על: מזמינים ומשנים פגישה. המטרה היא להזמין, לסרב בנימוס ולסכם סידור חדש. אפשר לבקש הסבר קצר בעברית או לחלק את המפגש.
teacher_script.say_en: We will practise a useful task step by step. You can ask me to repeat or explain. At the end, you will try a new version without the model.

teacher_script.say_he: לפני הדגם, נסה לומר באנגלית שתי כוונות שכבר פגשנו: לתכנן; חופשה.
teacher_script.note_he: רק אם הפריטים אכן נלמדו קודם; לאחר דילוג בעקבות מיון בוחרים מן הראיות האישיות.

teacher_script.say_he: צורת am/is/are עם ing יכולה לתאר גם סידור עתידי שכבר נקבע. כדי שיהיה ברור שלא מדובר בעכשיו מוסיפים זמן עתידי, למשל on Saturday. המשפט We are meeting at seven מתאר כאן פגישה שסוכמה, ולא רק אפשרות שאנחנו שוקלים.
teacher_script.text_en: We are meeting on Saturday at seven.
teacher_script.contrast_en: We are meeting now.
teacher_script.task_he: אישרתם עם בן פגישה בשבת בשבע. אשרו זאת באנגלית והתחילו ב־We are meeting.

ביטוי תמיכה לדגם: sounds good, במשמעות נשמע טוב. נלמד להפיק אותו בהמשך; עכשיו אפשר להיעזר בדגם.
ביטוי תמיכה לדגם: let me know, במשמעות עדכנו אותי. נלמד להפיק אותו בהמשך; עכשיו אפשר להיעזר בדגם.

teacher_script.text_en: Maya invites her friends to dinner at her home on Friday evening. Ben would like to come, but he has a work appointment at seven. He asks Maya if they can meet on Saturday instead. Maya is available then, but another friend, Noa, is visiting her parents on Saturday afternoon. Maya calls Noa and asks about the evening. Noa can come after six. They agree to meet at half past seven on Saturday. Ben is bringing a salad, and Noa is bringing juice. Maya is going to cook rice and chicken. She sends one message with the new day, time, and address. She writes, "Please let me know if you cannot come." The friends reply that the plan sounds good. They are happy they found a time for everyone.

teacher_script.text_en: Tom and Maya need a hotel for two nights. They look at two options. The Green Hotel is near the station. A room costs sixty pounds a night. The room is small, but it is big enough for two people. The Blue Hotel costs ninety pounds a night. Its rooms are bigger and more comfortable. It has a cafe, but the cafe is often crowded. It is also far from the station. Tom likes the Blue Hotel because he wants a comfortable room. Maya prefers the Green Hotel because it is cheaper and they can walk there. They are going to spend most of their time outside, so a large room is not important. After talking, they choose the Green Hotel. They can use the extra money for food and museum tickets.

postlesson.rubric_he: מילוי הכוונה, מובנות, התאמה למצב, שימוש עצמאי לפחות באחד מיעדי הפגישה. תשובה אחרת נכונה מתקבלת. זו משימה מתורגלת, לא הוכחת העברה לנושא חדש.
postlesson.hint_he: בחר משפט פתיחה מדגם השיחה; לאחר מכן נסה ללא הדגם.
postlesson.feedback_he: בחר נקודת יעד אחת לתיקון והפק שוב. בדיקת העברה נפרדת משתמשת בטופס חדש אחרי שלוש יחידות.

postlesson.prompt_he: תכנן את המשימה הבאה; בשלב הזה כתוב רק פתיחה ושני פרטים, או אמור אותם בקול: כתבו הודעה בת 50–70 מילים על היעדרות דמיונית ותור שנקבע. נסחו מחדש רק הנחיות שסופקו בטקסט, בלי להמציא טיפול.
postlesson.rubric_he: מילוי משימה, מסר ברור, סדר מתאים לרמה ודיוק ביעדים שנלמדו; אין תשובה יחידה.
postlesson.answer_anchor_en: I do not feel well. I have a cough and a headache. It started yesterday. Can I make an appointment? Could you say the time again, please?
postlesson.anchor_note_he: הדגם ממחיש שפה ומסר; הוא אינו פתרון יחיד או בהכרח תוצר באורך הכתיבה המבוקש.
postlesson.hint_he: תכנן כוונה, שני פרטים וסיום. במתחיל גם משפט אחד או אמירה בעל פה יכולים להיות שלב לימוד.
postlesson.feedback_he: ראשית בדוק שהמסר עובר; בחר עד שתי נקודות לתיקון וכתוב או הקלט גרסה שנייה.

lessons.completion_he: הוראה שבוצעה + לפחות ניסיון הפקה עצמאי אחד. השלמת פגישה אינה השלמת מילה או הסמכת רמה.

teacher_script.text_en: Ben does not feel well on Monday morning. He has a headache and a cough. He calls the health centre and asks for an appointment. The woman on the phone asks when the problem started. Ben says he started feeling ill on Sunday evening. She gives him an appointment at three in the afternoon. Ben sends a message to his manager. He says he cannot come to work today because he is ill. At the appointment, the doctor asks about his cough and checks his temperature. Ben listens carefully and writes down the instructions the doctor gives him. He asks the doctor to explain one word again because it is new to him. After the appointment, he goes home. He tells his sister that he hopes to get better soon.

Last week, he had his first conversation with a visitor at the station. He was nervous at first, but he gave the visitor the right directions. turns.text_en: Do I have to buy a ticket before I enter?

turns.text_en: Can I use my phone inside?

turns.text_en: Do I have to leave my small bag here?

turns.speaker: model

turns.text_he: לא. אין חובה להשאיר תיק קטן.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text_en: Where is the exit?
